task_2.title: Correct session-driven Vary header behavior
task_2.description: The session subsystem now marks responses as varying by cookies not only when session data is read, but also when the session cookie is removed or refreshed. This closes caching inconsistencies where cookie-dependent responses could previously be served without an appropriate `Vary: Cookie` header.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that responses affected by session state are marked with `Vary: Cookie` whenever the session is accessed, modified in a way that removes the session cookie, or refreshed, so caches do not treat cookie-dependent responses as generic.

expectation.grounded: In Flask session handling, `SecureCookieSessionInterface` should ensure the response includes `Vary: Cookie` whenever the session was accessed, whenever a modified session is emptied and its cookie is removed, and whenever `should_set_cookie` causes the session cookie to be written or refreshed. Existing `Vary` values should be preserved while adding `Cookie`.
expectation.conceptual: Any response whose behavior or headers depend on session cookies should advertise that dependency through `Vary: Cookie`, including read access, session clearing that removes the cookie, and automatic cookie refreshes.

constraints.grounded: Do not drop or overwrite unrelated `Vary` header members when adding `Cookie`. Do not introduce `Vary: Cookie` for requests where the session was neither accessed nor caused a session cookie write or removal.
constraints.conceptual: Preserve existing cache-variation rules while adding cookie variation only for responses that actually depend on session cookie state.

behavior: A response should include `Vary: Cookie` when request handling accesses the session, even if no session cookie is ultimately written.
A response should include `Vary: Cookie` when a modified session becomes empty and the session cookie is removed.
A response should include `Vary: Cookie` when the session cookie is written or refreshed, including refresh-only cases where the handler does not read session data.
If the response already has a `Vary` header, `Cookie` should be added alongside existing values rather than replacing them.
acceptance_criteria: When a request reads from or otherwise accesses the session, the response should include `Vary: Cookie`.
When a request clears or otherwise empties a modified session so that the session cookie is removed, the response should include `Vary: Cookie`.
When a request causes the session cookie to be reissued or refreshed without explicit session reads in the handler, the response should include `Vary: Cookie`.
When a response already varies on other headers, adding cookie-based session behavior should keep those entries and include `Cookie` in the same `Vary` header.
When a request does not access the session and does not cause a session cookie to be written, refreshed, or removed, it should not gain a new `Vary: Cookie` requirement from this change.

task_1.title: Werkzeug 2.3.3 compatibility for Flask test client sessions
task_1.description: Flask 2.2.5 updates test client session cookie handling so applications using Werkzeug 2.3.3 continue to save and reuse session state correctly while retaining compatibility with older Werkzeug cookie update behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Flask's test client continues to preserve session and cookie state correctly when upgrading to Werkzeug 2.3.3, without breaking compatibility with older supported Werkzeug releases.

expectation.grounded: When FlaskClient saves a session and applies response cookies back to the client, it must remain compatible with Werkzeug 2.3.3's _update_cookies_from_response call shape while continuing to work with Werkzeug 2.3.0 through 2.3.2 and environments that still use the older cookie jar extraction path. Session-related client flows should not fail with a TypeError during cookie synchronization, and the client's cookie state should reflect the response Set-Cookie headers for subsequent requests.
expectation.conceptual: Upgrading to this version should keep Flask's test client working across Werkzeug versions so that session changes made through client interactions continue to persist as cookies and remain available on later requests.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress cookie propagation in environments where FlaskClient uses Werkzeug's _update_cookies_from_response helper, and preserve the existing fallback behavior for environments where that helper is unavailable. Compatibility must cover Werkzeug releases with both the newer path-aware cookie update contract and the older contract.
constraints.conceptual: The compatibility fix must preserve existing session and cookie behavior across older and newer Werkzeug versions rather than only supporting one specific dependency version.

behavior: FlaskClient session-saving flows remain operational with Werkzeug 2.3.3 when response cookies are written back to the client.
When Werkzeug expects the newer cookie update contract, the client should update cookies using the request host, request path, and response Set-Cookie values.
When Werkzeug provides the older cookie update contract, the client should continue using that contract instead of failing.
When the Werkzeug cookie update helper is unavailable, the client should continue synchronizing cookies from the response through the existing fallback path.
acceptance_criteria: When an application uses FlaskClient to modify session state under Werkzeug 2.3.3, the session operation should complete without a TypeError and the resulting cookies should be stored on the client.
When a later request is made with the same FlaskClient after a session-changing response, the client should send the updated session cookie so the application observes the persisted session state.
When the same workflow runs against Werkzeug 2.3.0 through 2.3.2, cookie updates should continue to succeed using the older helper contract.
When the workflow runs in an environment without Werkzeug's cookie update helper, Flask should still synchronize cookies from the response using its existing fallback behavior.
